mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact the S&P 500 over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 6% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE exceeds 6% but S&P 500 returns are positive, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate coupled with high unemployment indicates economic stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive S&P 500 returns under these conditions invalidate this hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate during tightening cycles negatively impacts S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns during monetary tightening contradict this hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: High CPI inflation may lead to rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Negative CPI growth with positive S&P 500 returns would falsify this.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 1400 signals economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns with low HOUST invalidate this hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Employment growth with rising unemployment suggests inefficiency, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by 50k and UNRATE increases by 0.2pp
failure_condition: Positive returns under these labor conditions would reject this hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production in early-cycle expansion boosts S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns during early-cycle with high INDPRO growth would falsify this.
